title: Kenyan Tropical Fruit Tart
community: Urban Kenya — the bakery and hotel showcase dessert
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Tropical Fruit Tart — a buttery sweet pastry shell filled with a silky passion fruit crème pâtissière and decorated with a mosaic of fresh Kenyan tropical fruits. The most visually spectacular dessert in the Kenyan bakery and hotel repertoire.
longDesc: The tropical fruit tart is the dessert that stops people in their tracks at the hotel display counter — the mosaic of sliced mango, passion fruit, kiwi, strawberry, and pineapple arranged on a golden pastry shell filled with pale yellow passion fruit cream is extraordinarily beautiful.
steps: Make pastry: rub butter into flour and sugar. Add yolk and water. Press into a disc. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Roll and line the tart tin. Prick base. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Blind bake with baking beans at 180°C for 15 minutes. Remove beans. Bake 10 more minutes until golden. Cool.

Make crème pât: whisk yolks, sugar, and cornstarch. Heat milk to nearly boiling. Pour over egg mixture while whisking. Return to heat. Stir constantly until thick. Add passion fruit juice, butter, and vanilla. Press plastic wrap on surface. Cool.
Fill cooled tart shell with passion fruit cream.
Arrange fruit in a beautiful mosaic pattern.
Heat apricot jam with a little water. Brush over fruit for a glaze.
chefTips: The blind bake is essential for a crispy pastry base — skip it and the base is soggy.
Press cling wrap directly on the cream to prevent a skin forming.
Arrange the fruit by colour and size for maximum visual impact — this is an art.
commonMistakes: Skin on the cream — not pressing wrap.
Random fruit arrangement — this tart should be beautiful.
cookingScience: Blind baking dries the pastry base before the wet filling is added. Without this step, the moisture from the crème pâtissière soaks into the unbaked pastry during assembly, creating a soggy, underbaked base. The apricot glaze creates a pectin film over the fruit that seals in moisture and gives the characteristic glossy finish.
sustainabilityTips: All tropical fruits are locally produced in Kenya.
servedWith: As the centrepiece hotel display dessert
storage: Assemble on the day. Refrigerate up to 24 hours.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as a celebration dessert.
culturalNote: The tropical fruit tart is the dessert that represents Nairobi's bakery culture at its most beautiful — a classical French patisserie technique combined with Kenya's extraordinary tropical fruit abundance to produce something genuinely world-class.
